source.title: Allowed Origins (CORS) is ignored for webhooks with dynamic paths

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
**Bug Description**

For a Webhook node whose path contains dynamic parameters (e.g. `user/:id`), the node's Allowed Origins (CORS) setting is silently ignored. The lookup that resolves the configured origins compares the node's configured path with the concrete request path, and the two can never be equal for a dynamic webhook: a template like `user/:id` registers under `<webhookId>/user/:id`, while the request arrives as `<webhookId>/user/123`. When no node is matched, the CORS handling falls back to reflecting whatever `Origin` the caller sends, so any third-party page can read the webhook's response cross-origin. Static paths enforce the configured list correctly; only dynamic paths are affected. The same lookup problem exists in the test-webhook path, where the registration search also cannot resolve dynamic paths at all.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a workflow with a Webhook node (response mode "When Last Node Finishes").
2. Set the node's path to a dynamic template, e.g. `user/:id`.
3. In the node options, set Allowed Origins (CORS) to a fixed origin, e.g. `https://a.com`.
4. Activate the workflow and call the production URL `/webhook/<webhookId>/user/123` from JavaScript running on a different origin (e.g. `https://b.com`), and read the response.
5. Observe `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://b.com` in the response — the caller's origin is reflected and the browser allows the cross-origin read. The configured `https://a.com` is not applied.
6. For comparison, set the node path to a static value (no `:param`) with the same Allowed Origins: requests from unlisted origins now receive `https://a.com` in the header and the browser blocks the read.

**Expected behavior**

The Allowed Origins list configured on the node applies to dynamic-path webhooks the same way it applies to static paths: requests from an origin in the list get that origin echoed, and requests from any other origin get the first allowed entry in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (which the browser rejects) instead of a reflection of their own origin.

**Debug Info**

```
n8nVersion: 2.49.0 (source build, master @ 75fe21cb)
database: sqlite
n8n_executions_mode: main
consumerId: n/a (local source build)
```

The behavior is server-side logic and is not specific to this environment.

## Environment

**Operating System:** Windows 11 (affects all platforms; the issue is in the webhook handling, not platform-specific)

**n8n Version:** master @ 75fe21cb (2026-11-22), still present on current master (bf31087b)

**Node.js Version:** 24.20.0

**Database:** SQLite (default)

**Execution mode:** main (default)

**Hosting:** self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I traced this to the CORS-option lookup rather than the dynamic webhook dispatcher. `findWebhook(path, method)` can resolve the concrete request to its dynamic webhook row, but `LiveWebhooks.findAccessControlOptions` then searches workflow nodes with `parameters.path === path`. For a configured path like `user/:id` and a request for `user/123`, that lookup misses the node and returns no allowlist; the request handler then reflects the caller’s Origin. The test-webhook lookup also compares the configured node path directly to the concrete path.\n\nBoth lookups should use the resolved registration’s node identity (and, for test webhooks, the registration resolved by the dynamic-path matcher) to read that node’s options. That would apply the configured allowlist to dynamic paths instead of falling through to origin reflection.

comments.author: grinem
goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current source and found a concrete distinction from the proposed early-middleware diagnosis. `WebhookRequestHandler.setupCorsHeaders()` calls `findAccessControlOptions(path, method)`, and `LiveWebhooks.findAccessControlOptions()` resolves the webhook first, then still selects its node with `parameters.path === path`. A concrete path such as `user/123` therefore does not match the registered template `user/:id`. This method also dereferences `webhook.workflowId` without handling a missing result, so it is worth confirming whether the production request reaches this path or an earlier middleware in the reported setup. If it does, selecting the node from the resolved webhook registration (rather than comparing the template to the request path) appears to address the allowlist miss; separately verify whether the reflected-origin behavior comes from this handler or another CORS layer.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current source: `findAccessControlOptions()` resolves the webhook, but then matches the workflow node with `parameters.path === path`. For a concrete request such as `user/123`, that cannot match the configured template `user/:id`, so the node options (including its allowlist) are missed. The request handler then leaves CORS handling without those options. Can the lookup use the resolved webhook registration’s node identity rather than comparing the template with the request path? That would also avoid relying on path parsing a second time.

comments.author: Mattenhaim
comments.text:
Thanks @goutham-valugula, that matches what I found. #44772 implements exactly this:

- `LiveWebhooks.findAccessControlOptions` matches the node by the resolved registration's `webhookId` for dynamic rows, instead of comparing the configured path with the request path.
- `TestWebhooks.findAccessControlOptions` resolves the registration through the dynamic-path matcher and selects the node by the registration's node name.

Both cases have tests that fail on master. The missing-webhook dereference you mentioned is a separate, pre-existing issue, so I kept it out of this PR.
